answer.text: Whether prices react quickly and accurately to new information

explanation.text: The Logic: An event study measures the abnormal return around a corporate event (earnings releases, M&A announcements, dividend changes, regulatory actions) to assess whether prices react quickly and accurately to that new public information. Speedy, full price adjustment supports semi-strong EMH; sluggish or biased adjustment is evidence against it. The Trap: Studying only past prices is a weak-form test (runs, autocorrelation), not event studies. Insider trading studies test strong-form efficiency. Behavioural biases are separately tested through experiments and survey/transaction data, not event windows. Note: The NISM-Series-XXI-B Portfolio Managers workbook (Sep 2025) supports the broader semi-strong EMH statement that prices adjust rapidly and accurately to public information (around page 237), but does not name or describe the event-study methodology specifically. The framing above is general research-methodology knowledge.
